item.description: The dunnock (Prunella modularis) is a small passerine bird in the accentor family, Prunellidae. item.description: The magpie goose (Anseranas semipalmata) is a species of waterfowl found in northern Australia and southern New Guinea. item.description: The arc-eye hawkfish (Paracirrhites arcatus) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Cirrhitidae, the hawkfishes. It is found across the tropical Indo-Pacific, from East Africa to the central Pacific (including the Hawaiian and Pitcairn Islands), and from Japan south to Australia. item.description: Mary I (1516–1558) was the queen of England and Ireland from July 1553 until her death. item.description: The hyacinth macaw (Anodorhynchus hyacinthinus) is a parrot in the family Psittacidae, native to central and eastern South America. With a length of around 1 metre (3.3 ft), it is longer than any other species of parrot. It is also the largest macaw and the largest flying parrot species. item.title: Wikipedia picture of the day for March 25 - Wikipedia
item.description: The van der Grinten projection is a compromise map projection that is neither equal-area nor conformal. It projects the entire Earth into a circle, though the polar regions are subject to extreme distortion. The projection was proposed by Alphons J. van der Grinten in 1904, and, unlike perspective projections, is an arbitrary geometric construction on the plane. It was adopted as the National Geographic Society's reference map of the world from 1922 until 1988. Map credit: Strebe, using Geocart
